dossier.purpose: llama.cpp is a C/C++ inference engine for LLMs and VLMs built on the ggml tensor library (README.md:7,54-66). It loads GGUF models and runs them on CPU and many GPU backends (CUDA, Metal, Vulkan, HIP, SYCL and others; README.md:68-88). It ships the libllama C API (include/llama.h), a unified `llama` binary plus separate tools (CLI, bench, quantize, perplexity, RPC server), and `llama-server`, a local HTTP server with OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic-compatible APIs, a built-in Web UI, an optional router mode for several models, and an opt-in Prometheus-text /metrics endpoint (tools/server/README.md:7-20,1122-1146). Needs coverage (facts only): this repo has no OTLP receiver or exporter, collector, privacy filter, metrics/events/logs store, dashboard, or trace/dataset/experiment store (grep for otlp, opentelemetry, telemetry over src, ggml, common, tools/server, docs and CMake finds nothing). Of the six needs, the only one it provides is a local model server (llama-server with a CUDA backend whose default arch list includes sm_89, the RTX 4090 architecture).

claims.claim: Quick-start options: visit llama.app, run with Docker, download pre-built binaries from the releases page, or build from source.
`llama cli -hf ggml-org/Qwen3.5-0.8B-GGUF` downloads and runs a model from Hugging Face; `llama serve -hf ...` launches an OpenAI-compatible API server.
Goal: LLM (and VLM) inference with minimal setup and state-of-the-art performance on a wide range of hardware, locally and in the cloud.
Plain C/C++ implementation without any dependencies.
Apple silicon is a first-class citizen, optimized via ARM NEON, Accelerate and Metal.
Custom CUDA kernels for NVIDIA GPUs (HIP for AMD GPUs, MUSA for Moore Threads); Vulkan and SYCL backend support.
CPU+GPU hybrid inference to partially accelerate models larger than the total VRAM capacity.
Server provides OpenAI-compatible chat completions, responses and embeddings routes, and Anthropic Messages API compatible chat completions.
Server has monitoring endpoints; GET /metrics is a Prometheus-compatible exporter that is only accessible if --metrics is set.
By default the server listens on 127.0.0.1:8080; /health is public (no API key check).
MCP: the server can expose tools coming from MCP servers; only the stdio transport is supported; experimental, do not enable in untrusted environments.
Router mode: launching llama-server without a model exposes an API to load/unload several models and routes each request by its model name (default: up to 4 models loaded).
--offline: forces use of cache, prevents network access.

The only WSL mentions are docs/backend/OPENCL.md:39 (OpenCL, 'Ubuntu 22.04 WSL2 with Intel 12700H') and docs/docker.md:177 (SYCL Docker: 'WSL support has not been verified yet'); no WSL CI job found. platforms.macos_arm64: yes - README.md:58 (Apple silicon first-class); Metal is on by default on Apple (ggml/CMakeLists.txt:95-96; docs/build.md:140-145); pre-built llama-<tag>-bin-macos-arm64.tar.gz built on macos-26 with embedded Metal library and deployment target 13.3 (release.yml:70-73,132,1961); installable via Homebrew, MacPorts (sudo port install llama.cpp), Nix, conda-forge (docs/install.md:3-9,54-58); CI: build-apple.yml (ctest -L main at :101) and self-hosted M-series Metal CI (ci-self-hosted-metal.yml:49).
platforms.gpu: yes - NVIDIA CUDA backend (README.md:62,75; docs/build.md:155-182; ggml/src/ggml-cuda). RTX 4090 = compute capability 8.9 (docs/build.md:212); default arch list adds 89-real for CUDA >= 11.8 (ggml/src/ggml-cuda/CMakeLists.txt:34-38) and 'native' is used when GGML_NATIVE and CMake >= 3.24 (:27-28). GGML_CUDA is OFF by default, so a source build needs -DGGML_CUDA=ON (ggml/CMakeLists.txt:199). Pre-built Linux CUDA archives ship the CUDA runtime libs in separate cudart tarballs to extract next to the binaries (release.yml:429-448,1972-1973). -ngl defaults to auto and --fit defaults to on (common/common.h:473-481). CI evidence: build-only for 89-real (build-cuda-ubuntu.yml:73-81) and runtime tests on a T4 (ci-self-hosted-cuda.yml:48); no RTX 4090 runtime job found. Per-op CUDA support matrix: docs/ops/CUDA.csv (docs/ops.md:7).

integrations.cli: Unified `llama` binary with subcommands serve, cli, download, update (installer builds only), version, licenses, help; hidden: completion, bench, batched-bench, fit-params, quantize, perplexity (app/llama.cpp:64-78; app/CMakeLists.txt:3-4). Separate binaries: llama-server (tools/server/CMakeLists.txt:61-67), llama-cli (tools/cli/CMakeLists.txt:19-23) and the other tools under tools/ (tools/CMakeLists.txt:17-44), ggml-rpc-server only with GGML_RPC (tools/rpc/CMakeLists.txt:1). Python converters convert_hf_to_gguf.py etc. (pyproject.toml:28-32). Configuration via flags, LLAMA_ARG_* env vars (tools/server/README.md:304-335) and config.ini files at /etc/llama.cpp and ~/.config/llama.cpp (common/arg.cpp:716-735).
integrations.mcp: llama-server is an MCP client/host, not an MCP server. With --mcp-servers-config or --mcp-servers-json (Cursor-style mcpServers JSON) it spawns stdio MCP servers, sends initialize, tools/list and tools/call JSON-RPC, and exposes tools as <server>_<tool> to the Web UI and GET /tools; experimental and off by default (tools/server/README.md:353-387; tools/server/server-mcp.h:19-125; server-mcp.cpp:255-326). No /mcp endpoint is registered (tools/server/server.cpp:244-374). The Web UI can also reach remote MCP servers from the browser, with an opt-in --ui-mcp-proxy CORS proxy (tools/server/README.md:203,385).
integrations.sdk_or_api: C API include/llama.h (docs/build.md:3) plus C++ RAII wrappers include/llama-cpp.h (CMakeLists.txt:282-284). HTTP API from llama-server (tools/server/server.cpp:244-309): OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions, /v1/responses, /v1/embeddings, /v1/models, rerank, /v1/audio/transcriptions; Anthropic /v1/messages and /v1/messages/count_tokens; native /completion, /infill, /tokenize, /props, /slots, /metrics, /lora-adapters and router /models endpoints. Auth via Authorization: Bearer or X-Api-Key (tools/server/server-http.cpp:260-282). Python package gguf (gguf-py/pyproject.toml:1-10). Example apps for Swift and Android under examples/. No official HTTP client SDK found.
integrations.claude_code_or_codex: No documented Claude Code or Codex integration (grep for claude, codex, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL in docs and READMEs finds none; the only README mention is 'Prefilling of assistant messages similar to the Claude API', tools/server/README.md:17). Code-level compatibility only: Anthropic Messages /v1/messages and /v1/messages/count_tokens (tools/server/server.cpp:268,285) accepting x-api-key (server-http.cpp:272-276); a Claude-Code-specific shim that rewrites the cch= hash in an x-anthropic-billing-header system block so prefix caching still works (tools/server/server-chat.cpp:312-346, applied at :359,364; reference to PR 21793); an OpenAI Responses endpoint /v1/responses implemented by converting to chat completions (tools/server/README.md:1461-1501; server.cpp:264-265); tests tools/server/tests/unit/test_compat_anthropic.py (29 test functions) and test_compat_oai_responses.py. No repo text ties the Responses endpoint to Codex. The repo also ships contributor-facing CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md and skills/ (add-new-model, code-review) for AI assistants working on the repo itself; these are not a runtime integration.

readme.telemetry_and_network: No telemetry, analytics, crash-reporting or phone-home code found: grep for otlp, opentelemetry, telemetry, analytics, sentry over src, ggml, common, tools/server, tools/cli, app, docs and CMake finds nothing; the only hit is HF_HUB_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 in the example script examples/llama-eval/llama-eval.py:42. The Web UI has no analytics code and its version checks are same-origin (tools/ui/src/lib/stores/version.svelte.ts:40,52). No account is needed to run; HF_TOKEN / --hf-token is optional (tools/server/README.md:104). Network use is on demand: (1) model download via -hf/-hff/-mu/-dr or the *-default presets: default endpoint https://huggingface.co/ (override with MODEL_ENDPOINT or HF_ENDPOINT, common/common.cpp:1554-1567), Docker Hub registry (common/download.cpp:846,906), User-Agent llama-cpp/<build-info> (download.cpp:302-303,441-442); --offline / LLAMA_ARG_OFFLINE limits model downloads to the cache (common/arg.cpp:687,3928-3933; download.cpp:471-485). (2) The server fetches http(s) URLs found in chat-request media fields, not gated by --offline (tools/server/server-common.cpp:1088-1103). (3) Opt-in --ui-mcp-proxy/--agent expose a generic /cors-proxy (tools/server/server.cpp:337-344; server-cors-proxy.h:22-75). (4) `llama update` (installer builds only) runs curl -fsSL https://llama.app/install.sh | sh (app/llama.cpp:26-41). (5) Build time: default builds download prebuilt Web UI assets from https://huggingface.co/buckets/ggml-org/llama-ui (scripts/ui-assets.cmake:431-500; CMakeLists.txt:138) and optional options FetchContent BoringSSL/LibreSSL/CCCL (vendor/cpp-httplib/CMakeLists.txt:42-126; ggml/src/ggml-cuda/CMakeLists.txt:62-73). (6) The Web UI lazy-loads a HEIC decoder from cdn.jsdelivr.net when needed (tools/ui/src/lib/utils/heic-to-jpeg.ts:4-6) and keeps chats and settings in browser IndexedDB/localStorage (tools/ui/src/lib/services/database.service.ts:16; settings.service.ts:70). Local observability only: logs to stdout/stderr, --log-file, --log-jsonl (tools/server/README.md:106-107); --log-prompts-dir writes each prompt to a file (debug, off by default; common/arg.cpp:3891-3901; tools/server/server-context.cpp:4281-4282); per-response usage and timings, timings_per_token, return_progress (tools/server/README.md:593-595,1395-1437); /slots on by default and /metrics (Prometheus text, pull) off by default (common/common.h:671-673).

llama-server executable; calls llama_server() in tools/server/server.cpp (route registration at :244-374; router mode in server-models.cpp).

code.architecture: Layers: (1) ggml/ - tensor library and backends under ggml/src/ggml-{cpu,cuda,metal,vulkan,hip,musa,sycl,opencl,blas,rpc,cann,hexagon,openvino,virtgpu,...}; backends can be static or dynamic (GGML_BACKEND_DL, docs/build.md:845); ggml/src/ggml-cuda has about 68 top-level .cu files (flash-attention, mmq/mmvq, etc.) plus template-instances; per-backend op support CSVs in docs/ops/. (2) src/ - libllama: GGUF loading (llama-model-loader.cpp), per-architecture graph builders (src/models/*.cpp, about 155 files), KV cache and memory (llama-kv-cache*.cpp, llama-memory-*.cpp), sampler, grammar, vocab/tokenizer, chat templates; public API include/llama.h. (3) common/ - llama-common: argument parsing (arg.cpp), model download and HF cache (download.cpp, hf-cache.cpp), Jinja engine and chat parsing (jinja/, chat*.cpp), sampling, speculative decoding, memory fitting (fit.cpp), presets (preset.cpp), logging. (4) tools/ - server (server.cpp routes; server-http.cpp over cpp-httplib; server-context.cpp slots and continuous batching; server-models.cpp router mode that spawns child llama-server processes; server-chat.cpp OpenAI/Anthropic/Responses conversions; server-task.cpp including Prometheus text; server-mcp.cpp and server-tools.cpp MCP client and built-in tools; design notes in tools/server/README-dev.md:46-74), cli, mtmd (multimodal), llama-bench, quantize, perplexity, rpc, ui (Svelte Web UI embedded at build time). (5) app/ - unified llama binary linking the *-impl libraries. (6) gguf-py/ plus convert_*.py and conversion/ - Python GGUF tooling. Also examples/, tests/, scripts/, ci/, .devops/ (Dockerfiles, Nix, SRPM specs).
code.packaging_and_release: Nightly: every master push touching C/C++/CMake/shader sources runs release.yml (release.yml:3-28), builds per-platform archives (macOS arm64/x64, Ubuntu x64/arm64/s390x CPU, Vulkan, CUDA 12.8 and 13.4 with separate cudart tarballs, ROCm, SYCL, OpenVINO, Windows including CUDA 12.4/13.4, Android, iOS XCFramework, UI tarball: release.yml:1961-2005), uses GGML_BACKEND_DL and GGML_CPU_ALL_VARIANTS on Linux (release.yml:199-207,402-411), tags b<commit-count> (.github/actions/get-tag-name/action.yml:15-18) and creates a GitHub prerelease (release.yml:1939-1946). All release/* archives get a GitHub build-provenance attestation through actions/attest@v4 (release.yml:1821-1824,1923-1927); no checksum or signature files are produced for them (the only sha256 file is dist.tar.gz.sha256 for the Web UI bundle on a Hugging Face bucket, ui-publish.yml:45-47). Versioned releases: manual make-release.yml runs scripts/make-release-checks.sh (successful release.yml run for the commit, ggml matches upstream, tag unused; :25-120), pushes an annotated vX.Y.Z tag, creates a non-prerelease GitHub release that links the nightly build and uploads nightly-tag.txt, and re-tags container images (make-release.yml:59-154). At this checkout v0.5.0 (packed-refs) and nightly tag b11146 (.git/refs/tags/b11146) point to the same commit. docs/release.md:38-55 describes the process differently (see claim_checks). Containers: ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:{full,light,server}[-cuda|-cuda13|-rocm|-musa|-intel|-vulkan|-openvino|-s390x], rebuilt daily (docker.yml:19-21,86-101; CUDA 12.8.1 and 13.4.1) with image digests attested (docker.yml:549-568). PyPI: gguf from gguf-v* tags (gguf-publish.yml:13-44). Third-party channels: Homebrew, conda-forge, Nix, MacPorts, winget (docs/install.md). Building the tag from source yields version 0.5.0-dev unless -DLLAMA_BUILD_IS_DEV=OFF (CMakeLists.txt:14-21; docs/release.md:43-46).

code.dependencies: No lockfile for C++. Vendored in vendor/: cpp-httplib, nlohmann json, stb_image, miniaudio, sheredom subprocess.h, plus hash code (sha1, sha256, xxhash, rotate-bits) (vendor/CMakeLists.txt:1-11; README.md:122-126); .gitmodules is empty. code.security_policy: SECURITY.md exists. Private disclosure program disabled until further notice; fixes are to be sent as public PRs (SECURITY.md:15-16). Otherwise reports go through a private GitHub security advisory with a working proof of concept and a 90-day window; maintained by volunteers on a reasonable-effort basis (:18-22,37). In scope: src/, ggml/, gguf-py/, tools/server/* excluding the Web UI, experimental features, router/MCP and DoS bugs (:41-58). 'Using llama.cpp securely' guidance: sandbox untrusted models and inputs; do not use the RPC backend or llama-server on untrusted networks (:60-94). An AI-powered code scan is mentioned (:24-28).

risks: Scope: no OTLP, OpenTelemetry, collector, privacy filter, metrics/events/logs store, dashboard or trace/dataset/experiment store exists in this repo (grep over src, ggml, common, tools/server, docs, CMake). Observability is limited to logs (--log-file, --log-jsonl), per-response usage and timings, /slots, and an opt-in Prometheus-text /metrics that is off by default (common/common.h:671-673) and whose gauges reset on each scrape (tools/server/server-context.cpp:4683-4685). Qualification helpers are local tools only: tools/llama-bench, tools/perplexity, tools/server/bench/speed-bench, scripts/tool_bench.py (JSONL plus heatmap), examples/llama-eval (writes llama-eval-state.json).

Security defaults: no API key by default, and CORS reflects any Origin with credentials (common/common.h:641-644; tools/server/server-http.cpp:332-334); the server itself logs a warning for this (tools/server/server.cpp:327-329). /health and UI assets are unauthenticated (server-http.cpp:251-258) and the Docker server image binds 0.0.0.0 (.devops/cuda.Dockerfile:125). SECURITY.md:92 advises against llama-server and RPC on untrusted networks. Experimental --tools (including exec_shell_command and write_file), --mcp-servers-*, --agent and the open /cors-proxy are excluded from vulnerability handling (SECURITY.md:48-52; tools/server/README.md:203-208; server-cors-proxy.h:22-75).

Outbound fetch from request bodies: llama-server downloads any http(s) URL placed in image_url, input_audio or input_video fields (10 MB and 10 s limits, no allow-list), and --offline does not gate it (tools/server/server-common.cpp:1088-1103; common/arg.cpp:687), so a reachable server can be made to issue requests from the host.

Supply chain and network at build and run time: default builds download the prebuilt Web UI from the Hugging Face bucket ggml-org/llama-ui, falling back to 'latest', verified against a SHA-256 fetched from the same origin (scripts/ui-assets.cmake:431-500; CMakeLists.txt:138); optional FetchContent of BoringSSL, LibreSSL and CCCL (vendor/cpp-httplib/CMakeLists.txt:42-126; ggml/src/ggml-cuda/CMakeLists.txt:62-73); -hf pulls weights from huggingface.co by default, and an HF repo containing preset.ini switches the server to router mode with that preset (common/common.cpp:1554-1567; common/download.cpp:744-750; arg.cpp:677-683; server.cpp:524-527 warns 'Unknown presets may be unsafe'); `llama update` pipes curl output to sh (app/llama.cpp:26-41); the Web UI loads a HEIC decoder from cdn.jsdelivr.net (tools/ui/src/lib/utils/heic-to-jpeg.ts:6).

Release integrity and process: release archives have a GitHub attestation (release.yml:1923-1927) but no checksum or signature files; the v0.5.0 GitHub release carries no binaries of its own, they live in nightly tag b11146 at the same commit (scripts/make-release-desc.sh:62-74; .git/refs/tags/b11146); docs/release.md:38-55 contradicts make-release.yml:89-114 and references llama-install.sh, which is absent from the repo; building the tag from source gives 0.5.0-dev unless -DLLAMA_BUILD_IS_DEV=OFF (CMakeLists.txt:14-21); semver labelling is still a TODO (docs/release.md:24-25).

GPU validation and platform coverage: CUDA runtime CI runs on an NVIDIA T4 (ci-self-hosted-cuda.yml:48; server-self-hosted.yml:105, server tests not run on PRs at :161) and the only sm_89 job is build-only (build-cuda-ubuntu.yml:73-81); docs/docker.md:41 says GPU images are not tested beyond building. No RTX 4090 job or published RTX 4090 measurement was found in the repo. WSL2 has no CUDA documentation (only docs/backend/OPENCL.md:39 and docs/docker.md:177).

Interface churn: include/llama.h has 39 DEPRECATED( declarations and LLAMA_SESSION_VERSION 10 (include/llama.h:46); the server README lists removed flags (--draft-max, --draft-min, --spec-ngram-*, tools/server/README.md:284-288) and deprecated aliases (:2136); CMake options are being deprecated (CMakeLists.txt:186-195); router, MCP, built-in tools, --agent and tensor split mode are labelled experimental (tools/server/README.md:85,203-208). Scripts pinned to flags or saved state files may need changes between releases.

Maintenance and licensing: private vulnerability disclosure is disabled and the project is maintained by volunteers on a reasonable-effort basis (SECURITY.md:15-16,22); the server benchmark workflow is disabled (.github/workflows/bench.yml.disabled:1); AGENTS.md:51 bars fully autonomous agent contributions. Code is MIT (LICENSE, 'The ggml authors') and vendored libraries are MIT or public domain (README.md:122-126), but release binaries link OpenSSL or BoringSSL (release.yml:119,180) and the separate cudart tarballs redistribute NVIDIA libcudart, libcublas and libcublasLt (release.yml:439-442), which carry NVIDIA's terms rather than MIT.
